_readme: THE CONTINUOUS-IMPROVEMENT LEDGER for indianfminsights.site. One entry per check, defect or change made to the site. A run that changes the site must add a line here; if this file has no entry for a date, the site was not worked on that day. Never record a credential here - name a tool or a file, never a token.

gsc_loop.state: ON - Search Console is returning query rows since 3 Nov 2026, so the demand read is no longer empty
gsc_loop.note: The skill said to record the first week that returns rows. That date was never written down until 12 Nov 2026, which is why the loop looked dead. It is recorded now and this entry is the switch-on.

ga4.note: The Analytics connector is authorised but again returned no account and no property (an empty response on 18 Nov 2026). Sessions stay unmeasurable and are never estimated. Setting up GA4 is Swati's call, not a run's.

defects_found.what: markets.html kept the heading 'Markets - Monday 9 November 2026 close' after the 11 Nov brief rewrote the numbers underneath it.
defects_found.root_cause: No checker. The brief was hand-built each evening, so a dated string that was not rewritten shipped silently.
defects_found.fix: Heading corrected, and tools/site_check.py now fails any body date older than the published session.

defects_found.what: The 11 Nov brief was published as SIX separate commits (16:46:02 to 16:46:15), one file per commit, so for those 13 seconds the homepage and markets page disagreed.
defects_found.root_cause: The write step committed per file instead of per run. Same on the SEO files (2 commits on 11 Nov).
defects_found.fix: The rule is now one atomic commit per run covering every file the run touches. This commit follows it.

defects_found.what: The Market News page carried 20 stories dated 27-29 September 2026 - six weeks stale - under a snapshot that refreshed daily.
defects_found.root_cause: Nothing measured the age of the cards, and no job owned the news page.
defects_found.fix: Rebuilt with 8 verified stories dated 7-12 Nov 2026, each linked to its source. tools/site_check.py now fails if the newest card is older than 14 days.

defects_found.what: October CPI (6.09%, above the RBI's 6% ceiling) was published at about 16:05 IST, before the 16:30 refresh, and the brief still said the data was 'due later in the day'.
defects_found.root_cause: The brief was written from the 15:30 close and nothing re-read the tape between writing and publishing.
defects_found.fix: The post-close print is now carried on the markets page and the news page, attributed to NSO, Business Standard and BusinessLine.

defects_found.what: There was no site-side log of improvements at all: the skill's CHANGELOG records reel/lab work only, so the site looked like it never improved.
defects_found.root_cause: The 16:30 job had no script, no guard and no ledger - unlike the reel pipeline, which has all three.
defects_found.fix: This file, plus tools/site_check.py, plus the rule that a run which changes the site must log here.

defects_found.what: 16 pages - lessons, all 8 calculators, glossary, FAQ, about, search, privacy and 404 - still carried the 22 October 2026 close in their site-wide ticker (Nifty 22,687.65, Sensex 73,249.39, gold 1,48,070) while the homepage showed 12 November. A reader moving from the homepage to any lesson saw two different markets.
defects_found.root_cause: The brief job only ever wrote the three pages it considered 'the brief'. The ticker snapshot lives on every page, and nothing owned it. The first version of tools/site_check.py checked three pages too, which is why it did not catch this.
defects_found.fix: All 16 pages now carry the same snapshot as data/market.json, and site_check.py now checks EVERY .html file that carries a snapshot, not just the three brief pages.

defects_found.what: tools/site_update.py restamped EVERY sitemap lastmod and EVERY feed <updated> with today's date, so 42 unchanged article and calculator pages claimed a 17 Nov change and three feed entries shared one timestamp.
defects_found.root_cause: update_sitemap used a blanket <lastmod> replace and update_feed a blanket <updated> replace with no page or entry scope, and neither touched the feed entry's title or summary - a stale summary with a fresh stamp.
defects_found.fix: update_sitemap now restamps only index.html, markets.html and news.html; update_feed now rewrites the feed-level <updated> and the first (market-brief) entry's title, timestamp and summary from the payload. The 17 Nov commit carries the corrected sitemap (3 pages moved, 42 untouched) and a rewritten feed entry.

defects_found.what: markets.html shipped the keyfact with a literal '—' and a literal 'This page is education, not advice:' visible to the reader, and the currency row of the bullion table with a literal '·'.
defects_found.root_cause: render_markets_brief and render_markets_bullion ran every brief field through _esc() and nothing un-escaped the four inline tags and two entities the page actually uses, so the payload's markup reached the browser as text.
defects_found.fix: New _rich() helper: escape first, then re-permit only , , , , · and — - no attribute, no href, no script. Applied to headline, both paragraphs, the keyfact and the bullion note.
defects_found.status: fixed, guarded by eye - site_check.py has no assertion for visible entity text yet, and adding one is the next guard to write

defects_found.what: news.html carried a hand-written market snapshot table, note and heading that nothing refreshed: on the morning of 18 Nov it still read 'Market snapshot - 17 November 2026 close' with Tuesday's five levels, while every other page had moved.
defects_found.root_cause: The news page's snapshot was built by hand on 12 Nov and never given a marker region, so site_update.py had no way to reach it. The same class of defect as D1 and D3: a dated block outside every owned region.
defects_found.fix: The block is now a NEWSNAP marker region rendered from the same payload as every other figure (render_news_snapshot), and the markets page <h2> 'Markets - ... close' - which had also drifted back to the previous session's date - is now a HEAD region (render_markets_head). site_check.py's body-date rule caught the heading within one run of it reappearing.

defects_found.what: update_sitemap and update_feed still contained the blanket regexes that D3 (17 Nov) records as fixed: a global <lastmod> replace and a global <updated> replace. Only the files themselves had been corrected by hand, so tonight's run would have restamped 42 untouched pages and given all four feed entries one timestamp.
defects_found.root_cause: D3's fix was applied to the sitemap.xml and feed.xml output, not to the code that produces them - the ledger said 'fixed, guarded' while the defect was still one run away from returning.
defects_found.fix: update_sitemap now restamps only index.html, markets.html and news.html by matching each <loc> pair; update_feed replaces the feed-level <updated> (count=1) and rewrites the first entry through _feed_entry. Verified this run: 42 lastmods left at 2026-11-06, 3 moved to 2026-11-18, and the three non-brief feed entries left at 2026-11-13.

open_items.item: The lesson, calculator, glossary, FAQ and about pages all carry the same 22 Oct 2026 stamp.
open_items.why_it_matters: A single shared stamp across five pages reads as templated, and it is 3 weeks old.
open_items.owner: needs a decision - these pages change only when the content changes, so the stamp should be per page, not shared

open_items.item: 27 lesson pages share identical footer, disclaimer and related-lesson blocks.
open_items.why_it_matters: The shared sentences are boilerplate, not duplicated lessons - the lesson bodies are distinct. But the identical closing blocks are what makes the library read as repetitive.
open_items.owner: a design decision, not a data fix

open_items.item: what-is-ipo.html was recrawled by Google on 17 Nov 2026 11:52 UTC and came back 'Crawled - currently not indexed'.
open_items.why_it_matters: The page is the site's best demand signal (25 impressions, average position 54.6). It is no longer a crawl-lag problem - Google fetched the current page and chose not to index it, so the next lever is content quality and internal links, not another resubmission.
open_items.owner: needs Swati's decision - this job can measure it and must not fix it by adding words to a lesson

open_items.item: No page of the site carries the ARN-366695 / NSE AP-2069591891 disclosure block that the social captions carry.
open_items.why_it_matters: The footer says 'Educational only - not investment advice', but the MFD registration line that AMFI's master circular expects in all communication is absent from the website itself.
open_items.owner: needs Swati's decision - it is a compliance line, not a data fix, and a run must not invent a registration number

improvements.what: Sunday carry refreshed across all 46 snapshot-bearing pages: the weekend sentence now reads 'Markets are closed today, Sunday 15 November 2026' everywhere instead of Saturday 14 November, and the snapshot build stamp moved to 15 Nov 16:30 IST. The five levels are unchanged because the last session is still Friday 13 November 2026, and all five were re-verified from two same-dated sources before the carry (NSE close file + Moneycontrol/Hindu BusinessLine; BSE via PTI + Moneycontrol; Reuters + ECB reference rate; IBJA PM + Rozbhav/TrendRipperX/Niharika Times). site_check.py PASS; sitemap lastmod deliberately left at the session date 2026-11-13 so the site never claims a fresher session than it has.

13 Nov brief committed in one atomic commit. The 28 lesson pages still carried a 22 Oct snapshot (Nifty 22,687.65) - six weeks stale, and outside the 3 pages the 12 Nov fix covered; all 46 snapshot-bearing pages now share data/market.json. IBJA's 13 Nov AM benchmark replaces the 12 Nov figure, and the duplicated note paragraphs in the markets bullion panel were removed.
Added tools/site_check.py - cross-file consistency, dated-string, sitemap, feed and staleness checks against data/market.json as the single source of truth.
Market News rebuilt with verified stories from 7-12 Nov 2026 and a 14-day freshness rule.
Recorded the Search Console switch-on date (3 Nov 2026) so the demand loop is visibly running.

Monday-close refresh: all 46 snapshot-bearing pages, the homepage lead and glance table, the markets brief, movers, bullion, key points and sources, the news snapshot strip plus three new 16 Nov cards, the sitemap lastmods and the feed entry moved in one commit. Bullion is labelled as IBJA's 12:00 IST AM benchmark because the 17:00 IST print lands after the 16:30 job runs - the first time the brief has published an AM bullion print, and it says so.

markets.html kept the heading 'Markets - Friday 13 November 2026 close' after the numbers were rewritten: the same D1 defect class, on a string outside every marked region. Corrected in the same commit. site_check.py caught it, which is what D1's guard was for.

Tuesday-close refresh: all 46 snapshot-bearing pages, the homepage lead and glance table, the markets brief, movers, bullion, key points and sources, the news snapshot strip plus three new 17 Nov cards (the three 13 Nov cards dropped to hold the page at 14 stories), the sitemap lastmods for the three market pages only, the rewritten feed entry, seo-weekly and tech_watch in one commit. update_snapshots now walks every .html file instead of the three market pages, so the 46 baked snapshots cannot drift apart again. Bullion is IBJA's 12:00 IST AM benchmark, labelled, because the 17:00 IST print lands after this 16:30 job.

Wednesday-close refresh: all 46 snapshot-bearing pages, the homepage lead and glance table, the markets heading and brief, movers, bullion, key points and sources, the news page's snapshot block (now rendered, not hand-written) plus three new 18 Nov cards (the two 11 Nov cards and the 7 Oct RBI card dropped to hold the page at 14 stories), the sitemap lastmods for the three market pages only, the rewritten feed entry, seo-weekly and tech_watch in one commit. Three defects fixed on the way: D8 (escaped entities visible on markets.html), D9 (news snapshot and markets heading outside every owned region), D10 (the D3 blanket-regex fix existed in the output, not in the code).
